attribution.note: Marcus states this expectation in his own voice.

semantics.note: The firm expectation concerns further public reports of agent brittleness throughout 2025.

contract.note: Numerous reports spread across 2025 is an ordinary reading. The absence of an exact count does not prevent assessment, but a few examples cannot establish the full claim.

evidence.note: An April 2025 hands-on report documents scheduling failures; it establishes one qualifying report.
The May 2025 benchmark reports substantial agent failures, despite stronger results on some tasks.
The June report conveys an analyst assessment of current agent limitations. Its separate 2027 cancellation prediction is not an observed outcome.
The July 2025 article reports a concrete agent failure involving database deletion.

reviews.rationale: Four qualifying reports from April through July support the forecast's direction, but do not establish numerous reports throughout 2025. The packet supplies no later-year reports despite mentioning them in its gap statement. This limited sample also cannot establish that few reports existed.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the firm 2025–2027 forecast and narrow-use exception. The separately hedged decade forecast is properly excluded.

contract.note: Broad economy-wide knowledge work is an ordinary reading of the stated scope. Support must await the end of 2027; broad realized automation could contradict it earlier.

evidence.note: The October 2025 benchmark predates evaluation and measures remote-project capability, not the economy-wide share of knowledge work actually performed by agents.

reviews.rationale: The forecast runs through December 2027. The packet provides no broad realized-work measurement meeting the early-contradiction rule, and limited benchmark performance cannot establish support before the deadline.

attribution.note: Marcus makes and endorses the long-term prediction himself.

semantics.note: The knowledge-work and value predictions are firm, with an indefinite, distant horizon. Physical labor remains explicitly tentative and is not scored.

contract.note: Large-scale knowledge work and trillions in agent-attributable value are reasonable plain readings. No finite period of nonachievement alone could establish permanent failure of this undated prediction.

evidence.note: The dated benchmark concerns current remote-project performance. It measures neither eventual economy-wide automation nor agent-attributable value.

reviews.rationale: No deadline is stated, and the packet establishes neither a large realized share of knowledge work nor trillions in value. Low near-term benchmark performance cannot contradict the distant forecast. The tentative physical-labor extension is not adjudicated.

attribution.note: Marcus directly predicts that the scheduling feature will be unreliable.

semantics.note: The preceding reference identifies ChatGPT Tasks as the target. The prediction is firm despite the accompanying statement about what scheduling needs.

contract.note: Repeated missed, mistimed, or altered tasks fairly operationalize unreliable scheduling. This qualitative reading is ordinary, though it does not establish a population-wide failure rate.

evidence.note: The independent hands-on review documents a reminder displaced by 12 hours and repeated task alterations, meeting the review component of the early-resolution rule.
Dated first-hand reports describe missing notifications and unexecuted tasks. These are self-selected user accounts, not OpenAI findings.
The December 2025 user report describes continued scheduling failures. It supplies additional anecdotal corroboration, not a measured failure rate.

reviews.rationale: The April hands-on review and repeated dated user reports satisfy the contract's early-support rule. The review also describes useful experiences, and forum reports are self-selected, but those limitations do not negate the documented scheduling failures under the fair qualitative reading.
